subject: Clarify coverage: Type II attestation for runtime variants & evidence list
messages:
From: Anika Rao <compliance@finexa.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Cc: Marcus Lee <auditor@brightaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Type II coverage questions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Finexa's vendor due diligence we need to confirm the scope of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and collect supporting artifacts. Our risk team is specifically trying to understand which runtime components are covered by the Type II period (we need clarity for procurement sign-off):

- Does the current Type II period cover requests served from Hosted API only, or does it also include Dedicated GPU pools and Private/VPC connectors?
- For Dedicated pools: are dedicated pools that are tenant-isolated (reserved, single-tenant assignments) included, or only shared dedicated pools?
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments: do you provide an attestation or bridge for customer-managed connectors, or are those explicitly out of scope?

Can you provide a list of artifacts we should expect (report PDF, bridge/attestation text, network diagram, tenant mapping, KMS usage logs, retention policies, sampling guidance for Type II)? Also, our auditors (Marcus Lee, cc'd) will need machine-readable evidence where possible.

Target for procurement: we need to close this the week of Aug 23. Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Head of Third-Party Risk
Finexa Bank

Attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
To: Anika Rao <compliance@finexa.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>, Marcus Lee <auditor@brightaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Type II coverage questions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments

Hi Anika —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answer up front: our Type II report covers our hosted runtime and the orchestration/control plane behaviors that impact multi-tenant hosted customers. Dedicated GPU pools that are provisioned as reserved, tenant-isolated instances are included in parts of the report where we operate the infrastructure; however, customer-managed Private/VPC connectors (where the customer owns the network and keys) are typically out of scope for the core Type II.

That said, we provide a formal attestation addendum that states which components are included and which are excluded for each customer. For many customers we also produce a "coverage addendum" that auditors accept as companion evidence.

Requested artifacts we can deliver by Aug 20 (subject to a short review):
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) covering period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30
- Coverage addendum / attestation text for Finexa (draft)
- VPC connector diagram (PNG/PDF) showing control-plane vs data-plane ownership
- Dedicated tenant mapping (CSV) showing tenant -> pool assignments (redacted)
- Example KMS access log slice (TXT) and explanation of key wrapping model
- Retention policy excerpt & where logs are stored (runbook link)

Couple of questions for your team so we can scope the attestation properly:
1) Do you require the Type II period to include any particular retrospective window (e.g., backfill to include Jan 2025)?
2) Will your auditor accept a coverage addendum + machine-readable tenant mapping + sample logs instead of full customer-managed connector evidence?

If that approach sounds acceptable I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with Kimberly (security engineering) and Rishi (product ops) this week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Compliance & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
To: Anika Rao <compliance@finexa.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>, Marcus Lee <auditor@brightaudit.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Type II coverage questions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments

Hi Anika —

Following up with the technical mapping you asked for so auditors can validate evidence formats. High-level notes:

- Hosted API: fully in-scope for SOC 2 Type II. We can provide the report (PDF) and supporting telemetry slices (request logs, deployment annotations) for the period.

- Dedicated pools:
  * Reserved single-tenant pools that are managed by Redwood and remain within our control plane and our monitoring/telemetry are included in scoped controls (we have examples in the report mapping).
  * Dedicated pools where the customer brings their own hardware or a completely customer-managed VPC (on-prem) are out-of-scope for the Type II. For those we produce a written attestation that lists the excluded components and recommended compensating controls.

- Private/VPC connectors: these are partially out-of-scope. The control split is: control-plane functions (provisioning, routing decisions) are within Redwood's operational logs and can be covered; customer-managed network segments and on-prem hardware are out-of-scope.

Evidence we will provide (formats in parentheses):
1) SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025-07-01_2026-06-30.pdf (PDF)
2) Finexa-Coverage-Addendum-draft.txt (TXT) — proposed attestation language you can share with Marcus
3) vpc-connector-diagram.pdf (PDF) — shows where control plane telemetry is captured
4) dedicated-tenant-mapping.csv (CSV) — mapping with non-sensitive tenant ids and pool IDs
5) kms-access-sample.txt (TXT) — sample of KMS call logs (timestamp + key-id + action)
6) retention_and_runbook_excerpt.txt (TXT) — paths and retention windows for logs and key material events

We will not be sharing full KMS keys or raw unredacted logs. If Marcus's audit requires full raw logs, we can coordinate a direct auditor access arrangement under NDA — we typically provide a short window of read-only access to an auditor VM with sampling scripts.

Proposed next step: Monica, I'll prepare the draft coverage addendum and the CSV mapping; please confirm the language and I will post the Drive link.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated-tenant-mapping.csv (stub), vpc-connector-diagram.pdf (stub)
From: Marcus Lee <auditor@brightaudit.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>, Anika Rao <compliance@finexa.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Type II coverage questions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments

Thanks — quoting Monica and Kimberly below for context.

On Thu, Aug 13, 2026 at 08:42 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example> wrote:
> Evidence we will provide (formats in parentheses):
> 1) SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025-07-01_2026-06-30.pdf (PDF)
> 2) Finexa-Coverage-Addendum-draft.txt (TXT)
> 3) vpc-connector-diagram.pdf (PDF)
> 4) dedicated-tenant-mapping.csv (CSV)
> 5) kms-access-sample.txt (TXT)
> 6) retention_and_runbook_excerpt.txt (TXT)

Quick notes from the auditor perspective:
- The coverage addendum must explicitly name the control families and the component boundaries (e.g., "Control objective X: applies to Hosted API; Does not apply to customer-managed on-prem connectors").
- A machine-readable tenant mapping is very helpful — please include a column for control-plane-observed-pool-id and a column for declared-customer-managed boolean.
- For KMS evidence: a 24-hour slice with request identifiers, truncated key IDs, and a signed manifest of why those requests were pulled is sufficient for sampling.

We can accept an attestation that is backdated to the Type II period if it describes the controls and evidence that were in place during the covered period. However, the attestation must be signed by an authorized Redwood executive and reference the report date range.

I'll plan to review the Drive artifacts once Monica/Kimberly upload them. If you want a short call to confirm artifact formats, I'm available Mon Aug 23 13:00-15:00 PT.

Regards,
Marcus Lee
BrightAudit Inc.

Attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
To: Anika Rao <compliance@finexa.com>, Marcus Lee <auditor@brightaudit.com>

Subject: Re: Type II coverage questions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments

Hi Anika / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the auditor guidance. Per Kimberly's list, we've uploaded the following to a secure share (link below) and attached a short sample of the artifacts:

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.example/finexa-evidence-2026
Uploaded artifacts (samples):
- SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025-07-01_2026-06-30.pdf (full report)
- Finexa-Coverage-Addendum-draft.txt (draft attestation; please review the control-family mapping at the top)
- vpc-connector-diagram.pdf (diagram with control-plane/data-plane delineation)
- dedicated-tenant-mapping.csv (sample mapping; tenant_id, pool_id, control_plane_pool, customer_managed)
- kms-access-sample.txt (24-hour slice with truncated key ids)
- retention_and_runbook_excerpt.txt (log retention windows and S3 paths)

Proposed attestation language (feel free to adapt):
"Redwood Inference hereby attests that the SOC 2 Type II report dated 2026-07-15 covers Redwood's hosted inference runtime and those Dedicated GPU pools that are provisioned and operated under Redwood's control plane. Customer-managed Private/VPC connectors and on-prem deployments are excluded from the core report; Redwood provides a coverage addendum that documents the control split and recommended compensating controls for those components"

If Marcus is satisfied with the formats, Monica and I can get an authorized signature on the coverage addendum and provide a DocuSign flow by Aug 20. Otherwise we can give Marcus a time-limited, read-only auditor access to the sampled evidence on Aug 23.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Compliance & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
